question: Holding the accepted Knight mechanical carrier, skeleton, skin, motion, cameras and CAA appearance fixed, does replacing monolithic mechanical-surface presentation with explicit complete drawable layers remove the dominant remaining presentation failures?

intervention.partition_rule: Aggregate target skin weights through the sealed Knight target-to-source skeleton mapping; assign each mechanical face to the source joint with maximum mean aggregated weight; if more than 30 non-empty groups exist, merge the smallest groups upward through the source-joint parent tree until at most 30 remain.
intervention.complete_drawable_rule: Render each face group independently with the same posed M/G/W and same immutable CAA texture, thereby exposing drawable pixels that would otherwise be hidden by other groups.
intervention.static_order_rule: Derive one back-to-front drawable order per view from rest-pose mechanical depth pair evidence and keep it fixed for every animation frame.
intervention.dynamic_oracle_order_rule: Derive back-to-front drawable order per frame from privileged posed mechanical depth pair evidence.

interpretation.positive: A visible and measurable reduction of the known Knight presentation defects under either drawable variant supports missing drawable representation / overlap arbitration as a causal presentation bottleneck.
interpretation.static_only_or_static_matches_dynamic: A fixed drawable stack is sufficient for the tested frames.
interpretation.dynamic_beats_static: Pose-dependent draw-order arbitration is additionally required.
interpretation.negative: This mechanics-derived drawable oracle is insufficient. This does NOT falsify artist-authored drawable partitioning because the partition is mechanical rather than artist-authored; it instead points to drawable partition quality, deformation-domain binding, appearance completion, or carrier geometry as remaining causes.
